The gate scores CelesTrak's OWN published Segment-01 SupGP elements via the SAME SGP4 over the SAME source-OEM states our fit used, and requires ours <= theirs. This is the honest apples-to-apples comparison the packet gate text intends; the raw 0.071-vs-CelesTrak-reported-0.067 number is NOT apples-to-apples (0.067 is CelesTrak's in-sample RMS against their own ephemeris realization, not reproducible on our OEM — see rmsGapRootCause). tolerances.rmsGapRootCause:
A2.4c RESOLUTION (supersedes A2.4b). Two independent findings, both from measurement (native + WASM harness, evidence in the A2.4c worker report):
(1) FITTER CONVERGENCE — genuinely improved. The primary Levenberg-Marquardt plateaus at ~1.6 km on the sparse 4-min ISS arc (49 pts) and the Nelder-Mead rescue (Phase 5) lands at 0.080 km but stops SHORT of the true minimum because no LM pass follows it. A2.4c adds Phase 7: a final Gauss-Newton/LM polish that runs only when a derivative-free phase (NM/DE) produced the best result. It walks the residual surface to the local floor — ISS 0.080 -> 0.071 km — and is byte-identical for fits already at their LM minimum (all 10 Starlink beatsCelestrak cases unchanged; sub-metre fixture fits unchanged; Phases 5-6 never fire there). Monotone (strict-improvement-only, converged never downgraded), provider-agnostic (trigger is the solver path, not the source).
(2) THE 0.067 IS NOT MEASURED ON OUR FIXTURE — so it cannot be honestly beaten. Measured achievable SGP4 floor on our OEM by fit window: 1.6h 0.033 / 2.4h 0.056 / 3.2h (2-orbit, production) 0.071 / 4.8h 0.101 / 6h (CelesTrak's segment) 0.118 / 12h 0.38 km. RMS grows monotonically with arc length (SGP4 model error accumulates); a shorter window would trivially beat 0.067 but that gives WORSE forward-prediction elements = faking, forbidden by the directive. DECISIVE TEST: propagating CelesTrak's OWN published Segment-01 elements against our identical OEM scores 0.111-0.119 km (3.2h: 0.111, 6h: 0.119) — NOT 0.067. So CelesTrak's reported 0.067 is an in-sample RMS against THEIR ephemeris realization (issuance/sampling/TEME realization) that we cannot reproduce byte-for-byte, and on the SAME data our fit (0.071) already fits BETTER than CelesTrak's own elements (0.111). CONCLUSION: the honest apples-to-apples result is a win; the raw 0.071-vs-0.067 number comparison is not apples-to-apples. Per directive the gate stays honest elementRange — NOT faked to beatsCelestrak, tolerances NOT tuned. A2.4b's nutation ruling still holds (full 106-term IAU-1980; frame transform is not the cause).
